title: CAN BACKPLANE INTERFACE MEZZANINE BOARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: To build a mezzanine board to interface with a CAN bus on the units' backplane.Description:As part of the APA (Advanced Power Architecture) initiative, a standardised approach is being developed for internal communication between APA modules within an APA unit. This activity supports that effort by designing a compact, reusable TM/TC interface based on the CAN bus, known for itsreliabilityand simplicity.The mezzanine will serve as a common building block / solution for all APA modules, reducing integration effortandpromoting consistency across designs. By consolidating all required components into a small footprint, it simplifies system architecture, supports modularity and eases procurement, manufacturing and recurrence.This activity focuses on developing a compact mezzanine PCB that integrates five essential components required for CAN-based backplane communication (FPGA or microcontroller, ADC, voltage reference, CAN transceiver and XTAL/oscillator). The goal is to consolidate these elements into a small 30x30 mm footprint, supporting a range of external interfaces and operating on a 3.3V supply.This modular solution aims to simplify internal communication across systems where CAN is the preferred protocol, offering a reusable and scalable interface.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidate the CAN protocol implementation.- Architecture definition (evaluating if FPGA-based or microcontroller-based).- Identify two suitable options for each one of the 5 required components, prioritising compact packaging and cost.- Design a 30mm x 30 mm PCB accommodating the 5 components and ensuring signal integrity andmanufacturability, ready to be assembled into an APA module and to interface with CAN bus and the APA module.- Implement the software or the VHDL code with the CAN protocol.- Prototyping and testing, assemble and validate the board to confirm functionality and performance.Deliverables: Breadboard,ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: S3-SW-09 D3S END-TO-END SIMULATOR AND CONSTELLATION DESIGN
description: This activity aims to provide a key enabling tool to support the design and implementation planning of ESA's Distributed Space Weather Sensor System (D3S). The first part of the activity focuses on the development of a generic end-to-end mission simulator capableof assessing the performance of distributed space weather sensing architectures. The second part leverages the developed simulator to investigate and optimise the design of a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellation for space weather monitoring. Finally, the activity will assess and trade off different implementation options for the proposed constellation, including alternative payload configurations, dedicated satellites, and hosted payload opportunities

title: DISTRIBUTED TEMPERATURE AND STRAIN USING FIBRE OPTICS FOR THE CHARACTERISATION OF LARGE ANTENNA STRUCTURES - EXPRO PLUS
description: Large spaceborne antennas are increasingly required to provide large apertures while meeting stringent mass, dimensional stability and RF performance requirements. Examples include large active phased-array SAR antennas, reflectarrays and deployable reflector antennas. Thermally induced distortions, mechanical loads, deployment effects and long-term structural variations can result in changesof the antenna geometry which may affect the antenna RF characteristics.The knowledge of the actual antenna geometry and its evolution in orbit can therefore provide valuable information for the characterisation and prediction of antenna performance. Conventional temperature sensors provide measurements at discrete locations and do not directly provide information on structural strain or deformation. Similarly, direct geometrical metrology of large antenna structures may require dedicated instrumentation and may be difficult to implement in orbit.Fibre-optic sensing technologies offer the possibility of obtaining quasi-distributed (e.g. Fibre BraggGratings, Fabry-Perot)  and distributed (e.g. Rayleigh, Brillouin and Raman scattering) measurements over large structures with lowsensor mass and limited electrical harnessing. However, their application to large spaceborne antenna structures requires addressing several aspects, including temperature-strain discrimination, sensor integration and routing, spatial resolution, environmental compatibility and reconstruction of the structural deformation from the measured quantities.Previous work has demonstrated the use of fibre-optic strain measurements for shape reconstruction of large and deployable structures and antenna elements. In parallel, experience from large SAR antennas, such as Sentinel-1 and ROSE-L, shows the importance of accurate antenna-pattern knowledge and of accounting for antenna-pattern variations in instrument calibration and data processing.The present activity aims at connecting these two areas by investigating whether distributed/quasi-distributed fibre-optic measurements can provide sufficiently accurate knowledge of the thermomechanical state and deformation of a large antenna structure to support antenna characterisation and, potentially,antenna-pattern prediction or correction.The objective of this activity is to investigate, develop and experimentally validate afibre-optic sensing system for distributed temperature and strain monitoring of large spaceborne antenna structures.The activity shallassess fibre-optic sensing techniques capable of providing distributed measurements of temperature and mechanical strain and shall investigate methods for separating the two measurands.Methods to reconstruct the thermomechanical deformation of the antenna structure from the fibre-optic measurements shall be developed and validated. The impact of the reconstructed structural deformationontheantenna RF performance shall be assessed, including the feasibility of using the reconstructed structural state for antenna-patternprediction and compensation.A representative breadboard shall be designed, manufactured and tested under representative mechanical and thermal loading conditions.

title: VERIFICATION OF ADVANCED NAVIGATION ANTENNA - EXPRO+
description: Advanced satellite navigation antennas increasingly incorporate anti-jamming, anti-spoofing and adaptive beamforming capabilities to meet the growing demands of Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) applications. The verification of such antennas requires realistic Over-The-Air (OTA) test environments capable of reproducing complex signal scenarios with multiple simultaneous sources arriving from different directions. Existing test approaches are often limited in their ability to reproduce realistic operational environments, leading to lengthy test campaigns and reduced capability to assess the full radiated performance of advanced navigation antennas.State-of-the-art OTA test systems based on multiple transmitting elements have demonstrated the capability to emulate representative signal environments for navigation applications. Such systems enable controlled reproduction of satellite constellations, interference sources, multipath conditions and other operational scenarios in a laboratory environment. However, current solutions oftensuffer from limited flexibility, restricted angular coverage, significant infrastructure requirements or insufficient scalability to support future generations of advanced navigation antennas.A compact, scalable and flexible OTA radiated test system based on an arrangement of transmitting elements surrounding the Antenna Under Test (AUT) needs to be developed. The developed system shall provide the capability to emulate realistic navigation signal environments, enabling repeatable laboratory verification of advanced navigation antennas and associated signal processing techniques. The system is intended to support the development and validation of future PNT technologies and shall constitute a versatile test capability for advanced navigation antenna assessment.Equipment already available at ESTEC, such as a general waveform generator (e.g. PSG) and signal analyser (e.g. PXA), and necessary for this activity will be reused for test execution.The objectives of this activity are: Develop a scalable OTA architecture based on multiple transmitting elements arranged around the Antenna Under Test. Demonstrate the capability of the system to reproduce multiple simultaneous signal sources with controlled angular distribution. Validate the performance of the developed system through representative OTA test campaigns.

title: DETERMINISTIC ETHERNET SPACE TIME-SENSITIVE NETWORKING SOFT IP CORE - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a technology independent soft IP (Intellectual Property) core that complies with the aerospace profile of TSN(Time Sensitive Networking).Description:TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) and TTE (Time Triggered Ethernet) are the two technologies that allow to deliver determinism and quality of service on top of standard Ethernet networks. Since TTE can be considered  relatively closed technology (i.e. proprietary solution, patents pending on the technology), since a few years TSN is emerging as a potential successor of that technology. TSN is IEEE supported set of standards that implements wide range of quality of services (i.e. reliability, determinism, mixed criticality traffic, redundancy, time synchronization) on top of the standard Ethernet protocols. TSN benefits from Ethernet Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) tools/ecosystem, it is free of patents and is being introduced step-by step in industrial applications (automotive/industrial) and aerospace domain (IEEE P802.1DP - TSN for Aerospace Onboard Ethernet Communications). Although TSN is very successful in the automotive/industrial sector, in space applications TSNis still being considered as low TRL technology. Many current and future Exploration and Space Transportationmissions are considering Ethernet-based networks for the data-handling communication bus. Having thistechnology available for future ESA missions is seen as a key driver for future missions. The aim of this activity Is to develop an IP core that contains the core functionalities of Time-Sensitive Networking needed for space applications. Although the set of TSN standards is very wide, there are several on-going activities aiming attailoring of TSN for space applications. Having an TSN IP tailored to space applications could be considered asa key enabler of this technology in future ESA and national missions.The following technical aspects shall be considered:- Development of End-system IP Core. Switch IP core is out of scope of this activity- One or two Ethernet ports shall be supported.- Host integration: AXI4 lite for registers and IP configuration, and AXI4 stream for packet data- The IP shall support 10/100/1000Mbps speeds. 10Gbps is considered optional.- Compatible and configurable with various PHY interfaces (i.e. MII/GMII/RGMIII).- To be developed as technology independent VHDL.- To be implemented and validated in 2 FPGA/ASIC technologies (preferable NG-Ultra/Ultra300 andMicrochip Polarfire).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- TSN IP core requirements identification and development of the high-level architecture of the TSN soft IP core.- Prototype development and integration into a representative Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based network platform.- Verification and validation targeting high speed use cases- TSN soft IP core release and related documentation.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, SoftwareApplication/Need Date: Exploration and Space Transportation missions. Mission Classification: alpha, beta,gamma, delta
